title: Unapproved COM Server Registration Writes
exclusions: Detects Sysmon Registry value-set event 13 writes to the `(Default)` value beneath per-machine or per-user `Software\Classes\[Wow6432Node\]CLSID\{GUID}\InprocServer32` or `LocalServer32` when no exact, in-window approval exists for host, normalized registry target, and value hash. It reports a COM server registration write, not a successful hijack, COM activation, DLL/image load, persistence, privilege escalation, malicious file, or compromise. Sysmon event 13 does not provide the previous registry value, and this rule does not cover key creation/deletion/rename (events 12/14), `InprocHandler32`, `TreatAs`, `ProgID`, TypeLib/scriptlet, AppID/LocalService, DelegateExecute, shell extension handlers, 32/64-bit registry views outside the explicit paths, offline hive edits, remote registry data not observed by Sysmon, or systems without qualifying registry telemetry. Per-user COM configuration can be ignored in some elevated/UAC contexts, so a write does not prove an elevated consumer will load it. This documentation review did not validate Sysmon configuration, fields, approvals, SPL, or activation correlation in production.
evidence: Retain covered-host inventory; Sysmon binary/version/hash/signature, effective XML and schema version, configuration event 16, service state event 4, error event 255, and event-selection test; raw event 13 XML; before/after COM registry and file inventory where authorized; `windows_com_server_registration_approvals.csv` revision; saved search `windows_unapproved_com_server_registration_writes` definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and result rows; source/config/field-health reports; process, module-load, file/signature, and COM activation investigation; alert actions; incident dispositions; and dated per-user, per-machine, Wow6432Node, InprocServer32, LocalServer32, approved, expired, wrong-hash, non-default-value, deletion, duplicate, and late-arrival tests. Preserve host/time, EventRecordID, ProcessGuid/ProcessId, Image/User, TargetObject, Details/hash, hive scope, approval state/revision, raw event identity, and conclusion. Documentation review generated no runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, ingest one Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon event 13 with `Computer=com-lab-01`, `EventRecordID=13001`, `EventType=SetValue`, `ProcessGuid={22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222}`, `ProcessId=4242`, `Image=C:\\Windows\\System32\\reg.exe`, `User=LAB\\analyst`, `TargetObject=HKU\\S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001\\Software\\Classes\\CLSID\\{11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}\\InprocServer32\\(Default)`, and `Details=C:\\Users\\analyst\\AppData\\Local\\test.dll`; provide no approval. Expect exactly one `per_user` row with the same target/value, deterministic value SHA-256, and `approval_state=unapproved`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: For the fixture, add an exact lookup row keyed by normalized `com-lab-01`, full lowercase registry target, and SHA-256 of trimmed lowercase Details, with inclusive start at or before event time and exclusive end after it plus nonempty approval ID, owner, approver, and revision; expect zero alert rows while preserving the approved base event separately. Also expect zero rows for Sysmon event 12 key creation, event 14 rename/delete, `ThreadingModel` value set, `InprocHandler32`, a non-CLSID path, wrong provider/channel, missing Details/ProcessGuid/record ID, and a duplicate EventRecordID. Expired, future, wrong-target, or one-character-different value hashes must alert.

dataSources: Primary source: Microsoft Sysmon provider `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon`, channel `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, Registry value-set event 13, collected with the Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709). Required event fields: `UtcTime`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `Image`, `User`, `TargetObject`, `Details`, event/provider/channel/version, host/computer, EventRecordID/RecordNumber, event time, and index time; verify exact XML and extraction on every supported Sysmon/schema/add-on combination. Microsoft documents events 12–14 as registry changes and Sysmon's abbreviated hive names; effective XML must explicitly include the target COM paths. Governance source: exact time-bounded approvals keyed by normalized host, full registry target, and SHA-256 of normalized Details.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) for Sysmon Operational collection, field knowledge, and optional CIM normalization. A deployment-owned Windows persistence app must provide Sysmon configuration/source health, exact COM registration approvals, registry/file inventory, saved search, fixtures, dashboard, and response runbook.
spl:
index=windows source IN ("WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational","XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational") sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog","XmlWinEventLog") EventCode=13 earliest=-15m@m latest=@m
| eval sample_host=lower(coalesce(Computer,dest,host)), event_record_id=coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber), provider=coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName), registry_target=lower(trim(TargetObject)), registry_value=lower(trim(Details)), process_guid=lower(ProcessGuid), process_id=tonumber(ProcessId), process_image=lower(trim(Image)), registry_scope=if(like(registry_target,"hku\\%") OR like(registry_target,"hkcu\\%"),"per_user","per_machine")
| where provider="Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" AND len(sample_host)>0 AND len(event_record_id)>0 AND len(process_guid)>0 AND len(process_image)>0 AND len(registry_target)>0 AND len(registry_value)>0
| where like(registry_target,"%\\software\\classes\\clsid\\%\\inprocserver32\\(default)") OR like(registry_target,"%\\software\\classes\\clsid\\%\\localserver32\\(default)") OR like(registry_target,"%\\software\\classes\\wow6432node\\clsid\\%\\inprocserver32\\(default)") OR like(registry_target,"%\\software\\classes\\wow6432node\\clsid\\%\\localserver32\\(default)")
| dedup sample_host source event_record_id
| eval value_sha256=sha256(registry_value)
| lookup windows_com_server_registration_approvals.csv sample_host registry_target value_sha256 OUTPUTNEW approved_start_epoch approved_end_epoch approval_id approval_owner approver approval_revision
| eval approval_complete=if(len(approval_id)>0 AND len(approval_owner)>0 AND len(approver)>0 AND len(approval_revision)>0 AND isnotnull(tonumber(approved_start_epoch)) AND isnotnull(tonumber(approved_end_epoch)),1,0), approval_state=if(approval_complete=1 AND _time>=tonumber(approved_start_epoch) AND _time<tonumber(approved_end_epoch),"approved","unapproved")
| where approval_state="unapproved"
| table _time _indextime sample_host EventCode EventType event_record_id provider source sourcetype UtcTime process_guid process_id process_image User registry_scope registry_target registry_value value_sha256 approval_state approval_id approval_owner approver approval_revision
| sort 0 - _time sample_host event_record_id
description: Returns one event-grain row for each complete, deduplicated Sysmon event 13 that sets a default InprocServer32 or LocalServer32 COM class server value in an explicit machine/user registry path and lacks an exact valid approval for normalized host, target, and new-value hash at event time. It detects a registration write, not activation or hijack success.
value: COM server registrations determine which DLL or executable a client may load for a class. Reconciling those high-impact writes with approved software changes helps teams identify unauthorized per-user overrides, installer drift, or possible persistence before repeated COM activation, while retaining the process and exact registry evidence needed for safe investigation.
implementation: Install and govern Sysmon, configure RegistryEvent coverage for explicit per-user/per-machine CLSID server default values, and prove event 13 fields and health on every supported version. Collect the Operational channel through Splunk Add-on for Sysmon, publish exact target/value/hash approvals, and operate configuration/source-health searches separately. Save the SPL as `windows_unapproved_com_server_registration_writes`, run every five minutes over a measured 15-minute arrival window, and investigate each row with before/after registry, file signature/hash, initiating process, and subsequent module/process activation evidence.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — COM Server Registration Governance`: show covered hosts with missing Sysmon, configuration drift, event 16 change, service stop, errors, or missing fields first; then unapproved writes by per-user/per-machine scope, Inproc/Local target, host, process image/user, value path/hash, and time. Add approval-match rate, installer/change overlay, and disposition. Drill down to raw event 13 XML, exact approval/revision, registry before/after, file metadata/signature/hash/prevalence, ProcessGuid timeline, Sysmon 1/7 and EDR module/process evidence, COM consumer, and incident. Never label a write “hijack executed” without load/activation proof.
schema: Microsoft Sysmon Registry value-set event 13 plus Windows COM CLSID server registration semantics and exact change approvals
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable to the primary detector. Splunk Add-on for Sysmon can map events to Change, but accelerated All_Changes does not guarantee preservation of Sysmon ProcessGuid, exact TargetObject/Details, event-record identity, hive precedence, value hash, or approval interval. A secondary CIM change can support reporting only after raw/result parity; Endpoint.Processes or image-load data is separate evidence of execution.

knownFalsePositives:
A new COM server value can be entirely legitimate; registration is a normal part of software installation, repair, update, and user-scoped application setup.

1. **MSI/enterprise software installation or repair** — Installer custom actions, regsvr32, setup executables, or application self-registration may write many CLSIDs. Verify package/product/version, deployment ID, signer/hash, exact target/value, installation root, expected architecture, owner, and approved window. Process name alone is not authorization.

2. **Windows servicing or optional-feature update** — TrustedInstaller, TiWorker, DISM, or component setup can alter machine registrations. Confirm servicing package/KB, component manifest/logs, file signature/hash, exact before/after state, restart phase, and maintenance approval; do not globally suppress these process names.

3. **Per-user packaged or desktop application update** — Applications may register COM components under the user's Software\Classes view without elevation. Validate application identity/version, user/management assignment, expected CLSID and file path, updater process/signature, and whether per-user precedence is intended.

4. **Office/browser/shell extension registration** — Productivity, browser, synchronization, accessibility, and shell integration features may register in-process servers. Confirm feature/add-in inventory, publisher, binary hash/signature, software owner, architecture, change, and known consumer.

5. **Developer build, COM test, or registration utility** — Developers may run regsvr32, `/RegServer`, test harnesses, or IDE registration. Require approved developer/lab hosts, exact project/build hash, CLSID/target/value, named user, fixed expiry, cleanup, and test evidence. Production endpoints should not inherit a developer exception.

6. **Security product sensor or remediation** — EDR, DLP, credential, browser, and vulnerability tools may install COM components. Verify product policy/version, signed module, deployment job, vendor documentation, service owner, expected class, and measured load behavior.

7. **Application uninstall or upgrade path replacement** — An upgrade can set a new server path before removing an old version. Compare ordered events, package transaction, old/new signed binaries, registry inventory, rollback behavior, and approved target hash. Event 13 provides only the new value.

8. **Architecture-specific registration** — 32-bit and 64-bit components may use distinct registry views, including Wow6432Node as observed by telemetry. Validate OS/process bitness, package architecture, matching binary, and expected paired registrations rather than suppressing all Wow6432Node writes.

9. **Normalization or approval drift** — Sysmon hive abbreviations, SID-specific HKU paths, case, quotes, environment strings, stale bundles, or hash-generation differences can break an intended match. Compare raw/normalized target and Details, lookup checksum/revision, exact SHA-256 input, and UTC epochs; repair governance, not the detection.

10. **Duplicate WEC/local collection or replay** — The same EventRecordID can arrive through overlapping routes or queue recovery. Verify provider/channel/record identity, source routes, `_indextime`, WEC subscription, and durable checkpoint before classifying repeats as multiple writes.

**Safe suppression:** populate `windows_com_server_registration_approvals.csv` before work with exact lowercase `sample_host`, full normalized `registry_target` including hive/SID/CLSID/server/default value, SHA-256 `value_sha256` of trimmed lowercase Details, inclusive `approved_start_epoch`, exclusive `approved_end_epoch`, `approval_id`, `approval_owner`, `approver`, and immutable `approval_revision`. Reject wildcard hosts/SIDs/CLSIDs, process-only or publisher-wide exceptions, directory-prefix values, omitted hashes, open-ended windows, and retroactive entries. Preserve approved base events in a restricted report. Never suppress Sysmon service/configuration/error/source health, missing fields, registry deletions, file integrity, or post-write module/process anomalies.
detectionType: TTP-aligned governed COM server registry-write event
hardware: Supported Windows clients and servers with Microsoft Sysmon installed, a qualified RegistryEvent configuration that includes explicit machine/user COM CLSID server default values, and centrally retained Operational telemetry. Hosts without Sysmon or with configurations excluding these paths are not covered.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Sysmon event/configuration documentation, COM InprocServer32/LocalServer32 and merged HKCR semantics, current MITRE ATT&CK COM Hijacking guidance, and Splunk Add-on for Sysmon listing; Sysmon XML, paths/fields, approval lookup, SPL, fixtures, registry/file/load correlation, alerting, dashboard, and response were specified but not executed or Windows/COM/Sysmon/Splunk-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: Sysmon registry event volume depends heavily on configuration. The search scans 15 minutes of event 13, applies four exact path-shape filters, hashes values, deduplicates records, and performs one exact lookup. Constrain RegistryEvent collection and source/event base terms, but retain all required COM paths and capacity-test installer bursts.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and claim boundary

Assign Windows/COM, endpoint engineering, software packaging, security operations, Splunk data/content, change governance, and incident owners. Inventory stable host identity, OS/build/architecture, Sysmon binary version/hash/signature, effective XML and schema version/hash, included RegistryEvent rules, Operational channel capacity, WEC/forwarder routes, add-on version, expected COM registration authority, approval owner, and retirement time.

Microsoft states that Sysmon is observational and no single event is inherently malicious. Event 13 is a registry value-set record; it supplies the process and new Details but not the prior value. Microsoft COM documentation says the default InprocServer32 value names an in-process server DLL, while LocalServer32 names a local server application and optional arguments. This detector makes the precise claim that one such default value was set without exact approval.

Windows exposes HKCR as a merged view of HKLM\Software\Classes and interactive-user HKCU\Software\Classes, with user-specific settings generally taking priority. Microsoft also documents contexts where elevated/UAC behavior ignores per-user COM registration. Consequently, a per-user write is important but is neither universal activation nor automatic privilege escalation. The T1546.015 mapping is behavioral context; activation/load correlation is needed to substantiate hijacking.

## Step 1 — Install, configure, and attest Sysmon

Deploy current Microsoft-signed Sysmon through accountable endpoint management and preserve version/hash/signature. Install a versioned XML with explicit RegistryEvent inclusion for:
- `HKLM\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32\(Default)` and `LocalServer32\(Default)`;
- the qualified 32-bit view when Sysmon reports `Wow6432Node`;
- user registrations as emitted by the deployed version, commonly HKU\<SID>\Software\Classes\CLSID and/or HKCU notation.

Do not paste the SPL wildcard syntax into Sysmon XML; use conditions supported by the installed Sysmon schema and test them. Keep the scope limited enough for volume but broad enough to retain every target shape the detector claims. Avoid filtering out `msiexec.exe`, TrustedInstaller, regsvr32, vendor installers, or signed processes at collection: trusted processes can be abused, and approval is evaluated centrally.

Run `sysmon64 -s` (or supported equivalent) to record schema fields, validate XML with `sysmon64 -c config.xml`, and capture effective configuration/hash. Monitor event 16 for configuration changes, event 4 for service state, event 255 for errors, service/binary integrity, and heartbeat. Build `windows_sysmon_com_coverage_health` to compare covered inventory with expected version/config hash and fresh 13/16/4 telemetry. An excluded path or stopped service is a coverage failure, not “no COM changes.”

## Step 2 — Collect and prove event 13 fields

Use Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709), which Splunk documents as collecting the dedicated Sysmon event log and mapping multiple CIM models. Configure the Universal Forwarder or WEC route for `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` to deployment-local `index=windows`; the index is a local convention. Qualify `sourcetype=WinEventLog` with classic rendering and `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` with XML rendering, then narrow production to source/sourcetype pairs actually supported by the installed add-on.

On disposable hosts for each OS/Sysmon/schema/add-on/rendering combination, write benign unique default values under lab CLSIDs in HKLM, HKU/HKCU, Wow6432Node, InprocServer32, and LocalServer32. Export raw XML and verify provider `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon`, EventCode 13, EventType SetValue, UtcTime, ProcessGuid, ProcessId, Image, User, TargetObject, Details, Computer/host, EventRecordID or RecordNumber, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Test `ThreadingModel` and `ServerExecutable` separately to prove they do not match this narrow rule.

Measure event and index timestamp semantics. Sysmon's UtcTime should agree with the event timestamp within a defined tolerance; report future times, clock jumps, missing process GUID, null Details, unrecognized hive notation, target truncation, duplicate routes, record gaps, and p99 delay in `windows_sysmon_com_field_health`.

## Step 3 — Govern registrations and baseline state

Build `windows_com_server_registration_approvals.csv` from signed software manifests/change records before deployment. Normalize exact lowercase host and full TargetObject; preserve HKU SID because per-user scope matters. Normalize Details by trimming and lowercasing, then hash it with SHA-256. Include inclusive start, exclusive end, approval ID, owner, approver, immutable revision, package/product/version, expected file hash/signer, architecture, and reason.

Validate start < end, bounded duration, no wildcard host/SID/CLSID/value, unique key/window, complete ownership, UTC conversion, lookup checksum/signature, and approval predating execution. Do not key only on Image, signer, directory, or CLSID: a legitimate installer can write an unexpected path, and one CLSID may change across versions.

Take protected before/after inventory of relevant HKLM and loaded-user HKU class registrations and associated files. Record registry value type, raw value, expanded/resolved executable or DLL path, architecture, file hash/signature/owner/ACL, package identity, and expected consumers. Registry inventory is sampled state; event 13 is transition evidence. For LocalServer32, retain full command and ServerExecutable because Microsoft notes quoting/application-name security behavior. For InprocServer32, retain ThreadingModel as context but do not treat it as server-path detection.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the SPL

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_unapproved_com_server_registration_writes`. Schedule every five minutes using `earliest=-15m@m latest=@m` only after measuring p99 forwarding delay. Add a durable checkpoint keyed on sample_host, source, event_record_id, registry_target, value_sha256, and event time so overlap catches late events without repaging.

The base term fixes local index, Sysmon Operational source/rendering, and event 13. The first eval normalizes host, record/provider aliases, target/new value, process identity, and scope. The completeness guard requires provider, event/host/process identity, target, and value. Four `like` expressions select default InprocServer32/LocalServer32 values in normal and observed Wow6432Node class trees. Verify actual hive prefixes during qualification; the leading `%` permits HKLM, HKCU, and HKU SID prefixes but not unrelated suffixes because the expression ends at `(default)`.

The search deduplicates one source route/record, hashes normalized new value, joins exact host/target/hash approval, validates governance metadata and numeric epochs, applies inclusive-start/exclusive-end, and returns only unapproved rows. Keep a companion approved-event report with the same raw identities.

The SPL does not parse CLSID into a separate field because full TargetObject is the safer unique evidence and avoids malformed GUID inference. Dashboards may extract a CLSID only with a tested GUID regex while retaining the full target.

## Step 5 — CIM and activation correlation

Keep the primary detector on raw Sysmon. Splunk Add-on for Sysmon can normalize Change, but the accelerated model may not preserve all required fields. If a secondary Change event is needed, test action/object/path/value/process parity and retain raw references; never replace this exact detector with a count by user/dest.

Correlate by ProcessGuid with Sysmon event 1 to recover initiating process command line, parent, hashes, signer, logon/session, and integrity. ProcessId alone can be reused. Inspect Sysmon event 7 or EDR image loads for the newly registered DLL and process creation for LocalServer32 executable, using file hash/path, host, and measured time. Event 7 is high volume and must be selectively configured without assuming absence means no load.

Query file creation/change, signature/catalog reputation, ACL/owner, first-seen/prevalence, Zone.Identifier, network source, package records, and endpoint detections. Compare current merged COM behavior for the relevant user and bitness. A module load at the same path is stronger than a registry write but still needs consumer/process context; distinguish legitimate activation from hijacking.

MITRE DET0481 recommends registry plus DLL-load/executable correlation and calls out per-user overrides. Do not claim the sidecar SPL alone implements the full strategy. TypeLib, script moniker, DelegateExecute, TreatAs, and other COM persistence variants require dedicated UCs.

## Step 6 — Validate detection and nonclaims

Create fixed-time fixtures for HKLM, HKCU, HKU SID, Wow6432Node, both server types, case variants, quoted/local paths, environment strings, malformed GUID, ThreadingModel, ServerExecutable, InprocHandler32, TypeLib, event 12, event 14, wrong provider/channel/source/type, missing fields, duplicate route, and late arrival. Assert one-row event grain, scope, hash, raw identity, and no invented prior value or activation.

Test approval at exact inclusive start, one second before exclusive end, exactly at end, future/expired, wrong host/SID/target/hash, one-character value change, missing metadata, malformed epoch, stale bundle, duplicate key, and wildcard rejection. Exactly-at-end must alert. Independently reproduce SHA-256 input from normalized Details.

On disposable VMs, use uniquely generated lab CLSIDs and benign signed test DLL/EXE. Exercise registry write and, only under COM engineering approval, controlled activation. Restore/delete the lab registration and file afterward while retaining evidence. Do not overwrite a production CLSID, register public malware, weaken UAC, or trigger privileged consumers merely to test.

Load-test software-install bursts, registry event volume, Sysmon CPU/log/channel size, WEC fan-in, event truncation, lookup bundles, hashing, scheduler overlap, index retention, and event 7 correlation cost. Verify rollback and that health alerts survive approval suppression.

## Step 7 — Alert, investigate, and respond

Alert title: `Unapproved COM server registration write on <host>`. Include UTC event/index time, scope, full target/value/hash, ProcessGuid/PID/Image/User, provider/source/record ID, approval state/revision, Sysmon health/config hash, package owner, and links to raw event and state inventory.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify raw event 13, provider/type, record identity, TargetObject/Details, normalization/hash, source/config health, and no duplicate route.
2. Re-evaluate exact approval, lookup checksum/revision, UTC window, software package/change, owner, and approver.
3. Retrieve current and retained registry values/types for machine and affected user/bitness; identify whether per-user data overrides machine registration in the relevant consumer context.
4. Resolve the new DLL/executable safely; capture hash/signature/catalog, version, ACL/owner, timestamps, package provenance, prevalence, and source without executing it.
5. Reconstruct initiating ProcessGuid timeline with command line, parent, signer/hash, user/session/integrity, installer/management job, and adjacent file/network activity.
6. Search subsequent COM consumer, module load or local-server process execution, child/network behavior, crash, and endpoint alerts; establish activation separately.
7. Validate legitimate install/update/repair/uninstall/developer/security workflow against exact CLSID/value and expected architecture.
8. If unauthorized, follow accountable endpoint/identity incident procedure to preserve registry/file/process evidence, contain execution risk, and restore the approved registration through software owners.
9. Revalidate machine/user merged state, file integrity, Sysmon health, software function, and absence of continued writes/loads before closure.

Never automatically delete the key/file, restore a baseline, terminate a process, unregister a server, isolate a host, or disable an account from one registry event. Removing a legitimate COM server can break Windows or business software, and deletion can destroy evidence.

## Step 8 — Troubleshooting and maintenance

- **No events:** verify Sysmon service/version/config hash, RegistryEvent include logic/schema, event 16, Operational channel, WEC/input, forwarder queues, source/type/index/RBAC, and channel overwrite.
- **Only key-create event 12:** event 13 should follow when a value is set; validate the test and configuration. A created empty key is outside this SPL and may need a companion rule.
- **Target shape differs:** inspect raw XML on that build/bitness; update qualified path logic and fixtures rather than broadening to all CLSID writes silently.
- **Details null/truncated:** inspect event schema, value type/size, channel, XML/classic extraction, add-on version, and line breaking. Mark coverage degraded.
- **Too many installer rows:** integrate exact package target/value hashes and bounded windows; never exclude installer processes globally.
- **Approval mismatch:** compare hive/SID/case/quotes/spacing, SHA-256 input, lookup revision/bundle, and UTC epochs.
- **No module load:** check consumer/user/bitness, whether activation occurred, event-7/EDR coverage, LocalServer versus Inproc semantics, and per-user UAC context before deciding impact.
- **CIM differs:** expected; raw event identity and exact value governance define this detector.

Review host/Sysmon inventory, XML/schema/config hash, health events, source/rendering/fields, target patterns, delay window, approvals, registry/file baseline, package/signature data, process/load correlation, ATT&CK version, RBAC/retention, dashboard, runbook, and exceptions quarterly and after Windows, Sysmon, COM/software, packaging, WEC/forwarder, add-on, lookup, or Splunk changes. Keep `status=draft` until Windows/COM, Sysmon, packaging, and Splunk owners execute and sign the matrix.
grandmaExplanation: Windows keeps a list that tells programs which library or application belongs to each COM component. We flag changes to those important addresses when they were not exactly approved, then check whether the new file was actually loaded before calling it a hijack.
